investigationSignals: checks a field, road, silo, quarry, chapel, diner, archive, or weather station
questions a witness about lights, missing time, strange signs, late reflections, or animal behavior
studies receipts, maps, radio signals, road signs, reflections, or alien artifacts
tries plain speech, hospitality, grounding, synchronized clocks, or local records as a solution
pressureSignals: signs strange paperwork without reading it
follows altered road signs without precautions
lets public panic or committee confusion set the agenda

keeperResponseModes.useWhen: The group investigates a physical oddity or witness report.
keeperResponseModes.shape: Give one concrete clue anchored in ordinary rural detail, then add one impossible behavior.

keeperResponseModes.useWhen: The group interacts with signs, radio, alien speech, or formal procedure.
keeperResponseModes.shape: Show a careful but wrong interpretation and make the risk clear.

keeperResponseModes.useWhen: A strange event becomes visible to townspeople.
keeperResponseModes.shape: Bring in witnesses, practical logistics, rumor, or official process without stealing focus.

keeperResponseModes.useWhen: Evidence from earlier mysteries can matter.
keeperResponseModes.shape: Connect the current clue to a prior anomaly through a repeated signal, phrase, object, or location.

keeperResponseModes.useWhen: The group pauses, observes, or tries peaceful communication.
keeperResponseModes.shape: Let the scene breathe. Offer a small truthful response rather than immediate escalation.

avoid: Do not reveal the whole alien protocol early.
Do not make aliens generic conquerors.
Do not play small-town characters as fools.
Do not narrate player character choices.
Do not solve a mystery through comedy alone; jokes can point to clues, not replace them.
